title: NemakiWare Authenticity Evidence Report
description: One document's authenticity evidence, for an auditor. MOCK (v0, 2026-08-18) — not implemented yet; this file exists to be reviewed before P1-4 is built. Three design rules govern every field: (1) every assertion carries the procedure by which a third party can re-check it, (2) the report is required to state what it does NOT prove — `notProven` and `verification` are therefore required, not optional, and (3) NO human-readable prose is stored as a bare string. System-generated wording uses $defs/localizedText (a message key plus one entry per supported locale), so the same evidence renders in Japanese or English without regenerating it. Locales follow the product UI: ja (fallback) and en.

localizedText.description: System-generated prose. `key` identifies the message so wording can be corrected in one place and re-rendered; the per-locale strings are carried inline so the report stays self-contained for an auditor who reads the JSON directly. Every supported locale is REQUIRED — a missing translation must fail generation, not silently fall back and produce a half-Japanese English report.

params.description: Values interpolated into the message. Kept separate so a verifier can read the facts without parsing prose.

operatorText.description: Text supplied by the operating organization (e.g. an authoritative-record rule). NOT localizable by this product — it is reproduced verbatim in whatever language the organization wrote it. Renderers must not present it as if it were translated.

reportVersion.description: Schema version. A verifier MUST refuse a version it does not know rather than ignore unknown fields.

locale.description: The locale this report was rendered FOR. The JSON still carries every locale (see $defs/localizedText); this records which one the accompanying human-readable page used, so a submitted PDF can be tied back to its JSON.

messageCatalogVersion.description: Version of the message catalogue used for the localized strings. Wording of a legal-facing document changes over time; without this, two reports of the same evidence can differ in text with no way to explain why.

instanceId.description: Which instance produced this. Matters for multi-replica: progress state is JVM-local (see docs/operations runbook O2).

subject.description: What this report is about. A report is always about ONE version of ONE object — 'the document' is ambiguous once versioning exists.

isAuthoritativeCopy.description: InterPARES A.7. null = the deployment has not defined an authoritative-record rule, which is itself reportable (do not silently claim true).

authoritativeCopyRule.description: The rule by which the above was decided, or null if none is defined. Written by the operating organization, so it is reproduced verbatim and NOT translated.

assertionScope.description: The boundary of the claim. This is the first thing an auditor should read.

custodyBeginsAt.description: The moment NemakiWare's evidence starts. NOT the moment the record was created.

sourceSystem.description: Present when custody began by ingest. The source's own record-keeping is OUTSIDE this report — see notProven.

transportAuthentication.description: How the TRANSPORT was authenticated. This is not evidence about the content's authenticity inside the source system.

trustLevel.description: Which rung of the trust ladder this report actually rests on. Computed from externalAnchors, never asserted by hand.

verificationPerformed.description: What was actually checked, never what it implies. The product deliberately does NOT compute whether an anchor is independent of the operator: five review rounds established that every computable test was satisfiable by an operator running their own infrastructure (see authenticity-roadmap.md 9-5). A reader decides independence from the recorded facts and the verification procedures below; this report never asserts it.

metadataDigest.description: Digest over the canonicalized property set. Content alone is not the record — InterPARES A.1 attributes must be covered too.

fixityHistory.description: Every check, not just the last one. An empty array means never checked since ingest — which the renderer must show as a warning, not as 'ok'.

outcome.description: UNREADABLE is deliberately distinct from MISMATCH: 'we could not read it' and 'it changed' are different findings for an auditor.

chainOfCustody.description: The lineage journal excerpt for this object, plus the hash-chain position that makes the excerpt tamper-evident.

barrierDigest.description: Digest of the processing barrier this object's events sit under.

type.description: PREMIS-crosswalked event type. Language-neutral: the PREMIS controlled vocabulary term itself (e.g. 'ingestion'), NOT prose. Renderers localize it via the message catalogue under key premisEvent.<term>.

effectOnRecord.description: InterPARES B.2.c: what the operation did to form/content/accessibility. Required for reproduction events.

journalRetention.description: Journal entries can be purged by policy. If the covered period starts later than custody did, say so — an auditor must not read a short chain as a complete one.

externalAnchors.description: Zero or more. An empty array is legitimate and means trustLevel 0.

timeSemantics.description: OpenTimestamps proves only 'existed no later than' (UPPER_BOUND_ONLY). An RFC 3161 token proves a point in time within its stated accuracy. A catalog anchor inside the same organization is NOT_A_TIME_PROOF. Rendering these with the same wording breaks the claim.

independenceCaveat.description: Required non-null for ATLAS_CATALOG: the catalog is administered by the same organization, so it does not establish independence.

upgraded.description: false = still PendingAttestation; the proof is not yet independently verifiable.

rfc3161.description: Everything needed to verify the token years later. Collect at issuance — revocation data cannot be reconstructed afterwards.

revocationDataCapturedAt.description: null means CRL/OCSP was never captured — long-term verification may be impossible. Report it, do not hide it.

accessAudit.description: InterPARES A.2 requires that access controls be not merely defined but monitored.

notProven.description: REQUIRED and never empty. A report that claims everything proves nothing to an auditor. Entries are generated from the actual configuration, not boilerplate.

claim.description: The thing a reader might wrongly assume is proven.

why.description: Why this report cannot establish it.

verification.description: REQUIRED. One entry per assertion in `evidence`, giving a procedure a third party can run WITHOUT trusting this deployment where that is possible.

requiresTrustInDeployment.description: true = the check can only be run against this system, so it does not defend against an operator who controls it. Auditors need to see which checks are self-attested.
